description: Move a token to a new grid position on its scene.

reason.description: Optional; why the token moved, recorded with the move in the log. Only the DM and the agent read it: no player or spectator is sent it. At most 256 bytes of UTF-8; a longer reason refuses the whole move.

name: move_token

description: Add an actor to the campaign.

abilityIds.description: Optional. The abilities this actor has, each by its id in the served ruleset (get_ruleset lists them). use_ability refuses this actor any ability its sheet does not name, so an actor that names none can use none until give_ability gives it one; give_ability and take_ability change the list in play. With a ruleset served, an id the ruleset does not hold refuses the whole command, and an empty id refuses it with or without one. With a ruleset served, an ability that spends a resource the actor does not hold refuses the whole command: give the actor that resource too.

actorId.description: The new actor's id. Never reuse the id of an actor this campaign has had, even one since removed: a character log is named by its actor's id, so an actor added under a used id continues the earlier actor's log, if it had one, once it is a party member. At most 128 bytes of UTF-8; a longer id refuses the whole command.

attributes.description: The actor's numbers, each under a key the served ruleset declares as a number property (get_ruleset lists them); a sheet holds only the properties this actor has. With a ruleset served, a key it does not declare, or one it declares as a resource, refuses the whole command, and so does a key a catalogue form lists (get_ruleset's forms), whose value is its entries' and never a sheet's. At most 128 bytes of UTF-8 per name, and no empty name; either refuses the whole command.

controllerId.description: DO NOT SET. This command creates an actor; it does not hand it to anyone, and a request that sets this field is REFUSED whatever else it contains. Control is conferred by grant_actor_control, which also says whether the actor is a party member or a monster. Add the actor first, then grant it — two calls, always.

controllerIds.description: DO NOT SET. Refused, exactly as controllerId is, and for the same reason: control is conferred by grant_actor_control after creation, never here.

kind.description: REQUIRED. What this actor IS, which decides whether the whole party is told it exists. Set ACTOR_KIND_PARTY_MEMBER for a player's character, ACTOR_KIND_NON_PARTY for every monster, NPC and creature the party must DISCOVER by seeing it. There is no default and omitting it is REFUSED, because an unstated kind cannot be told from a deliberate one — if you are inventing a creature you already know which it is, so say so. Kind is not about who controls the actor: a character whose player is away is still a party member, and a monster you run yourself is still a monster. grant_actor_control states it again every time it grants control, and a creature a player is to run for a while is made a party member there, whatever it was added as.

moduleData.description: Optional; omit unless a rule module instructs otherwise — moduleData is opaque.

moduleId.description: Optional; omit unless a rule module instructs otherwise — moduleData is opaque. At most 128 bytes of UTF-8; a longer one refuses the whole command.

name.description: Optional display label for the actor. At most 256 bytes of UTF-8; a longer name refuses the whole command.

current.description: REQUIRED; the resource's present value, 0 included.

max.description: Optional; the resource's maximum. Left out or 0, it has none.

resources.description: The actor's resources, each under a key the served ruleset declares as a resource property (get_ruleset lists them), each giving its current, 0 included, and its max if it has one; a sheet holds only the properties this actor has. A resource whose current is null or left out refuses the whole command, and with a ruleset served so does a key it does not declare, or one it declares as a number; with a ruleset served, so does a resource some ability of the ruleset spends that no ability the actor names spends. At most 128 bytes of UTF-8 per name, and no empty name; either refuses the whole command.

name: add_actor

description: Place an actor's token on a scene's grid.

gmName.description: Optional; the DM's and the agent's alone: no player or spectator is ever sent it.

gmNotes.description: Optional; the DM's and the agent's alone: no player or spectator is ever sent it.

name.description: Optional; what every participant whose watched character sees this token is told it is, such as "a sleeping creature". Never the creature's true name unless the characters know it.

notes.description: Optional; what they are told of it beside its name.

tokenId.description: The new token's id, unique in the campaign. At most 128 bytes of UTF-8; a longer id refuses the command.

name: place_token

description: Rewrite a placed token's name, notes, GM name and GM notes, all four at once: a field sent empty is cleared, so send the present value of any you keep. Players and spectators whose character sees the token are sent its new name and notes; the GM name and GM notes reach only the DM and the agent. DM/agent only.
name: describe_token

description: Take a token off the board, for good. This is NOT hiding it — the piece is no longer part of the world going forward, for everyone at the table. It does not erase that the token was ever there; the log keeps whatever place_token/move_token history it had before this. DM/agent only.
name: remove_token

description: Take an actor out of the world, for good, along with every token it has on the board. This is NOT hiding it and NOT revoking control — the actor is no longer part of the world going forward, for everyone at the table, and there is no un-remove. It does not erase that the actor ever existed; the log keeps its add_actor and everything that happened to it. This ONE call also removes each of the actor's tokens, so do not call remove_token first. DM/agent only.
name: remove_actor

description: Start a new play session.

name.description: The session's title, shown to everyone at the table. At most 256 bytes of UTF-8; a longer name refuses the command.

name: start_session

description: End the current play session.
name: end_session

description: Use an ability the acting actor's sheet names (its abilityIds) against explicit targets. A use of any other ability is refused, whatever your role.

targetIds.description: The ACTOR ids of the creatures the ability is aimed at, never a token's id: a token is only where an actor stands on a scene, and an id that names no actor is refused. Each target must have a token in the caster's scene within the ability's range. A player's every target must be an actor the character judging their moves sees; any other is refused exactly as an id that names no actor is.

name: use_ability

description: Remove a named condition from an actor (DM-ended durations).
name: remove_condition

description: Give an actor one ability of the served ruleset (get_ruleset lists them): afterwards its sheet names the ability and use_ability resolves it for that actor, while the resource it spends lasts. An ability that spends a resource the sheet does not hold is given with that resource's value under resources, its current required, 0 included, and its max optional: the sheet then holds that resource too. Only its ability list and that resource change: its tokens, controllers, conditions, attributes and other resources stay as they are, so use this, not remove_actor and add_actor, to change what a character can do. Refused, appending nothing: an actor the campaign does not hold, an ability its sheet already names, an empty ability id; with a ruleset served, an id the ruleset does not hold, an ability given without the value of a resource it spends that the sheet does not hold, a resource the sheet already holds, and a resource the ability does not spend; with no ruleset served, any resources. Each player who controls the actor while it is a party member is told. DM/agent only.

abilityId.description: The ability's id in the served ruleset.

actorId.description: The id of the actor whose sheet changes.

current.description: REQUIRED; the resource's present value, 0 included.

max.description: Optional; the resource's maximum. Left out or 0, it has none.

resources.description: Only for an ability that spends a resource the sheet does not hold, and then required: that resource, under its name, with its current, 0 included, and its max if it has one. Any other resource refuses the whole command, and so does a current null or left out.

name: give_ability

description: Take one ability from an actor's sheet: afterwards its sheet does not name it and use_ability refuses that actor the ability, whoever asks. With a ruleset served, the resource the ability spends leaves the sheet with it when no ability left on the sheet spends it; no other resource leaves. Nothing else about the actor changes. Refused, appending nothing: an actor the campaign does not hold, and an ability its sheet does not name. Each player who controls the actor while it is a party member is told. DM/agent only.

abilityId.description: The ability's id in the served ruleset.

actorId.description: The id of the actor whose sheet changes.

name: take_ability

description: Add a story entry to the table's shared narrative — narration, in-character speech, or out-of-character table talk; optionally anchored to the event sequences it narrates. The DM and the agent voice anyone with `as`; a player speaks as a party member they control by `actorId`; `outOfCharacter` speaks as yourself, under the name the server writes.

actorId.description: A player's line in character: the id of a named party member they control, whose name the server writes as the speaker. Refused from the DM and the agent, and beside outOfCharacter.

anchorFromSeq.description: Optional; omit (0) if this narration is unanchored. Set together with anchorToSeq as a backward-pointing range (both > 0, anchorFromSeq <= anchorToSeq, anchorToSeq before this narration's own sequence) — never set one without the other.

anchorToSeq.description: Optional; omit (0) if this narration is unanchored. Set together with anchorFromSeq as a backward-pointing range (both > 0, anchorFromSeq <= anchorToSeq, anchorToSeq before this narration's own sequence) — never set one without the other.

as.description: Optional speaker label, the DM's and the agent's — set to voice an NPC or a PC in character; omit for plain narration. The server writes a player's speaker, and an out-of-character line's, itself.

outOfCharacter.description: Optional; set for table talk out of character. The server writes your own display name as the speaker; set no actorId with it.

name: add_narration

description: Whisper to one or more party members, or, as a player, to the DM. A whisper is written into the world log and into the log of each party member it names and no other, so only the DM and whoever watches through those characters read it. The DM and the agent name the party members in `toActorIds`; to whisper to a player, name every party member they control. A player whispers to the DM from a party member they control, named by `fromActorId`. Answer a party member's whisper to the DM with add_whisper, never add_narration, which every character hears.

fromActorId.description: A player's whisper to the DM: the id of a named party member they control, who whispers it. Refused from the DM and the agent, and beside toActorIds.

toActorIds.description: The DM's and the agent's: the ids of the party members who hear it, each a party member. Empty for a player's whisper to the DM.

name: add_whisper

description: Create or replace a keyed world note (locations, NPCs, quest state) — the campaign's durable memory.

visibility.description: REQUIRED. Who may read this note. NOTE_VISIBILITY_PUBLIC sends it to every player and spectator; NOTE_VISIBILITY_SECRET keeps it for the DM and the agent. There is no default and omitting it is REFUSED. Upserting a public note's key as SECRET removes it from every player's and spectator's view, though not from what they have read; upserting a secret one as PUBLIC sends it to them.

name: upsert_note

description: Delete a world note by key.
name: delete_note

description: Load a prepared adventure into the campaign — compiles its scenes, statblocks, notes, and opening narration into one atomic batch of setup events. DM/agent only.
name: load_adventure

description: Give a participant control of an actor, so they may move its token and use its abilities, AND state what that actor is while doing it. A grant makes a spectator a player: a participant who is neither the DM nor the agent is a player exactly while they control an actor. Such a participant may be granted only a party member (ACTOR_KIND_PARTY_MEMBER). A grant naming a participant the table does not hold, or has removed, is refused. Control is a SET — granting does not take control away from anyone who already has it, and an actor may be controlled by several participants at once. DM/agent only. Note the DM never needs this to act: DM authority is independent of control, so a DM already moves and uses any actor while a player controls it.

kind.description: REQUIRED. What this actor IS **right now**, which decides whether the whole party is told it exists. ACTOR_KIND_PARTY_MEMBER when you are assigning a character to the player who will run it, and when you are handing a player a creature to run for a while, such as one they summoned, one they possessed or one charmed into their service: while a player runs it, it is a party member, with a character log of its own that they may watch. ACTOR_KIND_NON_PARTY for a monster or NPC you run yourself, including one you take over to run. This is NOT about who is holding it: a character whose player is away is still a party member, and a goblin you are running yourself is still a goblin. It describes standing RIGHT NOW and it can change: when a player's run of a creature ends, revoke_actor_control them first and then grant it to yourself with ACTOR_KIND_NON_PARTY, or remove_actor it — a player may hold only a party member, so a non-party grant of an actor a player controls is refused. Revoking alone leaves it a party member.

name: grant_actor_control

description: Take a participant out of an actor's control set. Used to REASSIGN a character — when a player leaves the table for good, or a character changes hands — and to take a creature back when a player's run of it ends: revoke them first, then grant it to yourself with ACTOR_KIND_NON_PARTY, since revoking alone leaves it a party member. A player whose last actor is revoked is a spectator. Never used to let the DM act, which needs no revocation. DM/agent may revoke anyone; a player may revoke only themselves.
name: revoke_actor_control

description: Make a player a spectator: it revokes their control of every actor they control, one actor-control revocation per actor, as remove_participant does, and writes nothing for a participant who controls none. role accepts ONLY "spectator". A participant becomes a player when granted an actor (grant_actor_control), never by a promotion; someone who joined through the shared link arrives as a spectator and can only watch until then. A dm or an agent cannot be made a spectator. DM/agent only.
name: promote_participant

description: Remove a player or a spectator from the table for good. This cannot be undone: their credential stops working, every connection they have open is closed, their display name is free for someone else to join under, and they are no longer listed. It also revokes their control of every actor they control, writing one actor-control revocation per actor, so each is left to whoever else controls it, or to no one, until you grant it again. Use it for a participant who will not be back, such as the old identity of someone who joined again from a new browser. A dm or an agent cannot be removed this way. DM/agent only.
name: remove_participant

description: Open or close the table's shared join link. While it is OPEN, the next few people holding the link can join as spectators without an invite; while it is CLOSED the link is inert and admits nobody, which is how a campaign starts. door must be "JOIN_DOOR_OPEN" or "JOIN_DOOR_CLOSED" — leaving it unset is refused rather than guessed at, because guessing wrong either admits strangers or locks the table out mid-session. DM/agent only. Changes operational state, not the campaign, so it writes no event.

admitLimit.description: Optional; omit for the default of 8. How many people THIS opening may admit before the door stops letting anyone new in — a bound on what a leaked link can cost, since closing the door later does NOT revoke anyone already through it. Opening the door again starts a fresh budget.

name: set_join_door

description: Replace the shared join link's secret. Use this when a link has LEAKED: the old link stops admitting anyone, while everybody already at the table keeps their own credential and their characters. Independent of the door — rotating does not open or close it. DM/agent only. Writes no event.
name: rotate_join_link

description: Open the door at a scene square. Refused unless the square's tile is a door (maps-as-geometry spec §3.3, §6). actorId names the actor that opens it, any actor the campaign holds, or none. A player's door command is refused unless a token of a character of theirs stands beside the door. An actor the campaign does not hold is refused, once those checks pass, with: There is no such character.

actorId.description: Optional; omit for none. The actor that opens the door: any actor the campaign holds, wherever its tokens stand. An actor the campaign does not hold refuses the command.

name: open_door

description: Close the door at a scene square. Refused unless the square's tile is a door (maps-as-geometry spec §3.3, §6). actorId names the actor that closes it, any actor the campaign holds, or none. A player's door command is refused unless a token of a character of theirs stands beside the door. An actor the campaign does not hold is refused, once those checks pass, with: There is no such character.

actorId.description: Optional; omit for none. The actor that closes the door: any actor the campaign holds, wherever its tokens stand. An actor the campaign does not hold refuses the command.

name: close_door

description: Load a standalone map into the campaign — compiles its terrain and scenery into one SceneCreated plus one TokenPlaced per placement the map declares, atomically. DM/agent only. Unlike load_adventure, a map brings no actors, notes or opening narration — just terrain and placements; a placement's actor must already exist (add_actor it first) or the whole load is rejected.
name: load_map

description: Choose the character log this connection is sent: a spectator may watch any PARTY MEMBER, or nobody with an empty actor_id; a player may watch only the party members they control. The DM and the agent are refused, since they are sent the world. A monster or NPC is refused whoever controls it, with one message whether the actor exists or not. The switch is announced by a ViewpointChanged frame and followed by that log from its first entry. This is a view preference, not campaign history: it writes no event and is not visible to anyone else at the table.
name: set_viewpoint
